name: Maiquetía Simón Bolívar International Airport
before:
Venezuela's main international gateway, at Maiquetía in Vargas, serving Caracas, whose centre lies about 21 km to the west.

This is an airport where the route map needs checking before anything is promised. International services have been contracting for over a decade. KLM left in 2005 and British Airways stopped direct London flights the same year. Since 2014 foreign and domestic carriers have cut or ended services over political instability and an inability to recover 3.8 billion dollars owed to airlines. Some carriers schedule a stop in a neighbouring country so crews do not have to stay overnight in Caracas, which is considered unsafe. In November 2025 Venezuela withdrew operating permits from six airlines, Iberia, TAP, Avianca, LATAM Colombia, Turkish Airlines and Gol, after they suspended flights.

What remains reaches destinations in Central and South America with a few services to Spain, Russia and China.

Treat any schedule for this airport as provisional and verify it directly before booking.

It is commonly known simply as Maiquetía.
after:
Venezuela's main international gateway, serving Caracas from Maiquetía in La Guaira state, about 21 km north of the city. It is commonly known simply as Maiquetía.

Two earthquakes on 24 June 2026 damaged the terminal and stopped passenger flights. The airport reopened on 1 September from temporary terminals while the main terminal is repaired, at about a quarter of its usual capacity. Airlines were coming back in stages that month: Air Europa and Iberia from Madrid; American Airlines from Miami; Avianca and LATAM from Bogotá; and Copa from Panama City.

The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to most of Venezuela. Treat any schedule for this airport as provisional and verify it directly before booking.

claims.claim: carriers left from 2014 over instability and 3.8 billion dollars owed
claims.wasBefore: Since 2014 foreign and domestic carriers have cut or ended services over political instability and an inability to recover 3.8 billion dollars owed to airlines.
claims.why: History superseded by the 2026 returns. The 3.8 billion dollar figure is an old IATA number and was not re-verified.

claims.claim: crews avoid overnight stays in Caracas
claims.wasBefore: Some carriers schedule a stop in a neighbouring country so crews do not have to stay overnight in Caracas, which is considered unsafe.
claims.why: Only one solid dated source: Aviacionline (12 November 2025) reports TAP and GOL adding crew-change stops for security reasons. Reports from 2026 on the US airlines are speculation, and nothing shows which airlines do this since the September reopening. The FCDO advice now carries the safety warning.

claims.claim: permits withdrawn from six airlines in November 2025
claims.wasBefore: In November 2025 Venezuela withdrew operating permits from six airlines, Iberia, TAP, Avianca, LATAM Colombia, Turkish Airlines and Gol, after they suspended flights.
claims.why: Superseded. The Rio Times reports the episode ended gradually, with Air Europa back in February 2026, Plus Ultra on 3 March and Iberia on 6 April; AirInsight has Avianca back in February. Iberia, Avianca, LATAM Colombia and GOL were all returning in September 2026.
